schema_notes: Each company entry is ground truth for eval/run_eval.ts to compare pipeline output against.

Sourcing rule: every cited `source_url` is a company website page, an official registry, an official press release, or a news article that did its own original reporting. Aggregator/directory pages (Crunchbase, PitchBook, LinkedIn, Tracxn, Dealroom, Sacra, Seedtable, CB Insights, etc.) were used only to FIND candidate facts and leads during research — never as the cited source for a value here.
Never seeded from AlphaMap's own database — built independently so comparing against it is meaningful.

confidence per field: 'verified' (2+ independent primary/direct-reporting sources agree, or one lead-investor/company-direct source), 'likely' (one credible direct-reporting source, not independently corroborated), 'unknown' (no primary source found, or sources conflict with no way to resolve). Fields marked 'unknown' are excluded from precision/coverage scoring, not guessed.
hard_case_tags follow the v2 spec's categories (Section 6 / issue 13): common_name, non_us, rebrand_domain_change, series_a_start, stealth_no_data, went_public.

STATUS: human-reviewed batch of 2 (Apex, Fresha) remains final/reviewed. A second, NOT-yet-human-reviewed batch of 10 (listed in the v3 schema_note above) was added by Claude in this session, covering hard-case categories not in the first batch: non_us (Israel/Wiz & Fiverr, UK/Wise, Germany/Celonis, India/Zepto), rebrand_domain_change (Wise, Shortcut), series_a_start (Wiz, Celonis), stealth_no_data (Safe Superintelligence, Thinking Machines Lab), went_public (Fiverr, Wise), and common_name (Bolt, Mercury, Shortcut). All 10 need the same hybrid human review (city/country/founded_year/every funding round) before counting as final; reviewed_by_human is false on every one. The remaining target-batch companies continue in follow-up sessions.

v3 (this batch): added 10 more companies (bolt-checkout, wiz-security, fiverr, wise-transferwise, celonis, zepto, shortcut-software, safe-superintelligence, mercury-technologies, thinking-machines-lab), Claude-researched only (reviewed_by_human: false on all), same primary-sourcing rules as v2. Two new optional structural fields introduced and used where relevant: is_public_company ({value, confidence, source_url, notes}) to test the public/private boundary explicitly, and hard_case_notes (free-text) for hard-case context that does not fit an existing field (e.g. dual-HQ ambiguity, name-collision disambiguation, bootstrapped-to-Series-A narratives). Also introduced, used only where applicable: rebrand_notes (reused from v2 Fresha pattern), funding_rounds_excluded_unknown (reused from v2), ipo_status (zepto only, for a pending-not-yet-listed IPO case), and acquisition (wiz-security only, for an announced-but-not-closed M&A exit that is NOT a going-public event).

Batch 3 (2026-10-20): Claude-researched from search-result summaries only (pages could not be opened from the research sandbox), so every value needs the human review before it counts; confidence was set conservatively — 'verified' only where two independent direct-reporting sources agreed. New optional fields: batch (number), arr_usd ({value, as_of, confidence, source_url, notes}) for revenue scoring, and funding_rounds_excluded_unknown is now honoured by eval/score.ts (an extracted round matching one of them is neither right nor wrong). Round type 'Unknown' marks a round whose letter the sources contradict.

Batch 4 (2026-10-25): ten companies, Claude-researched from search-result summaries (pages could not be opened from the research sandbox), reviewed_by_human: false on all. Fills hard cases the first 22 lacked: Germany (Black Forest Labs, Parloa, Helsing), France (Mistral AI), India (Sarvam AI), UK (Synthesia, Wayve), a rebrand with a domain change (Vercel, ex-ZEIT), and two recent listings (eToro, Klarna). Rounds announced in euros carry amount_usd converted at the announcement month's rate, with the euro figure in notes. Review sheet: eval/review/batch4.md.

2026-10-25 — location policy (owner's decision, the Dealroom model): `country`/`city` are the headquarters TODAY; the new `founding_country` is where the company was founded (scored as its own field). Israeli-founded companies now headquartered abroad (Wiz, Cyera, Upwind, HiBob) carry founding_country Israel. Upwind's country moved from Israel to United States on that rule.

2026-10-26 (owner): three fields are now scored, each with its own Phase 1 bar (eval/score.ts PHASE1_BARS). round_type: judged on rounds matched to a verified golden round by amount and date — the existing funding_rounds[].type is the truth (debt rounds are typed Debt / Venture Debt); 'Unknown' output is missing, not wrong. competitors: {names, not_competitors, confidence, source_urls} — names a primary source says compete with the company; not_competitors partners, customers, investors and 'similar companies' a data platform lists; a name in neither is unjudged. patents: {numbers, none, confidence, source_url} — publication numbers from the EPO register / Espacenet where the company is applicant (any publication of a family counts); none: true when the register shows none. Companies without these two fields are not scored on them; the bars fail until enough companies carry them.

2026-10-27 (owner): competitors are judged on 20 companies (those carrying `competitors`), precision only — is every competitor v2 finds really one; no coverage. eval/run_eval.ts writes each unjudged competitor it finds to eval/review/competitors_review.csv with its source and quote; the owner marks נכון / לא נכון; eval/import_review.ts moves the marks here. Patents come from the EPO register: eval/patent_register_review.ts lists every publication for each company's name, the owner marks which are the company's (owner or filer), and eval/import_review.ts writes `patents` for each company whose rows are all marked.
